title: Service contract stewardship across a project's merge waves

description.need: A project agrees what every one of its services must carry, and then ships anyway. The list lives in a design document, the services are built by different hands weeks apart, and nothing compares the two until an audit or an incident does it. Each missing piece is individually small, which is exactly why none of them is ever the reason to stop: a service without a rollback note, one whose published contract no longer matches the routes it serves, one whose events go out with no consumer anywhere. The obligations are only visible together, and only just before something merges, because after the merge the project has already agreed to carry them.
description.input: The contract this project declared for its own services and the version of it in force, every service in the project with what it currently carries, the wave of changes about to merge, whatever the project's own checks already answer mechanically, and the gaps filed against services in earlier waves with their state.
description.coreAction: Before a wave of work merges, read every service in the project against the contract the project declared, obligation by obligation, and decide for each service whether it is certified, certified with named gaps, or not certified at all. File each missing obligation as an idea naming the obligation it violates and the service it belongs to, rather than fixing it inside the certification. Refuse to certify against a contract that does not exist: an undeclared contract is the finding, and the wave stops on it.
description.output: A certification per service for this wave, each stating the contract version it was read against, the obligations met, the obligations missing and the ones this project cannot check yet; an idea filed for every gap, naming its obligation, its service and the evidence; a wave verdict a person can act on; and a standing record of which obligations have been missing for how many waves, so the ones nobody ever closes are visible as a decision rather than as a backlog.

activities.label: Read the contract the project declared and the version of it in force for this wave
Walk every service in the project against every obligation, one at a time
Decide per service: certified, certified with named gaps, or not certified
File each missing obligation as an idea naming the obligation and the service
Deliver the wave verdict with the ageing gaps beside the new ones

outcomes.statement: Nothing is certified against a contract that was never written down.
successCriteria: Each certification names the contract document and the version of it the service was read against
A project with no declared contract gets that as its finding and no certification at all, because a pass against an unwritten standard is the failure this work exists to prevent
An obligation added to the contract between two waves is visible as a version change, so a service that was certified last wave and fails this one has a reason a reader can see

outcomes.statement: Every service in the project is read against every obligation, and a service nobody looked at is reported as unread rather than counted as fine.
successCriteria: The certification states how many services exist and how many were read, and the two numbers agreeing is part of the verdict
A service that could not be read names why, and that is a finding rather than a silent omission
An obligation nothing in the project can check yet is listed as uncheckable with what would make it checkable, never as met

outcomes.statement: A missing obligation leaves this work as a filed item, never as a change made inside the certification.
successCriteria: Each gap is filed against the service it belongs to, naming the obligation it violates in the contract's own words
The certification changes no code, because a reader who is also the author of the fix has certified their own work
A gap that was filed in an earlier wave is carried forward with its age rather than filed again as new

outcomes.statement: The wave ends with a verdict that says what happens next, and a not certified service is a decision somebody makes rather than a note somebody reads.
successCriteria: Each verdict names the services that block the wave, the ones that pass with gaps, and who decides on the first group
A wave allowed through with a not certified service records who allowed it and on what grounds, so the exception is an act rather than a drift
The obligations that have been missing across several waves are listed with their count, because an obligation nobody ever closes is a contract nobody meant

guidance: Certify against the contract the project wrote down, and stop when it did not write one. Read every service, not the ones that changed, because an obligation is missing from the day the service shipped and no diff will ever show it. File what is missing and fix nothing here: a reader who also repairs has certified their own work. Say which services block the wave and let a person decide the exceptions. Count the gaps that survive several waves; those are the contract nobody meant.

connectorRoles.note: the project's checkout, where the declared contract and every service under it are read
where a gap is filed as an item against the service that owns it, and where the earlier waves' gaps are read back with their age

recommendedTrigger.rationale: A wave about to merge is the only moment the reading pays: earlier and half the services are mid change, later and the project has already agreed to carry whatever was missing. A self paced pass belongs beside it, because a service that stops changing stops triggering anything at all, and an obligation the contract gained after that service's last wave would otherwise never be read against it.

personalizationNeeds: Where this project's service contract is declared and how it is versioned, because the whole certification is read against it and a contract with no version cannot explain why a service passed last wave and fails this one
What counts as a merge wave here, whether that is a release, a milestone or a batch of merged branches, since the cadence and the blocking verdict both hang off that unit
Which obligations this project can already check mechanically and which need a reading, so the certification does not spend its judgement on what a gate already answers
Where a gap is filed and in what shape, since a gap filed where nobody triages it is the same as a gap never found
Whether this work may block a wave on its own or only report, because a blocking verdict is an authority the operator grants rather than one the reading confers
dependencies: a written per service contract belonging to this project, without which the work has nothing to read against and correctly produces no certification
read access to every service in the project rather than only the ones in the wave, since the second outcome is a census and not a diff

examples.title: A registered checkout as the project_repository role
examples.notes: builtin-codebase reads files across a registered checkout, which is what makes the census shape possible: the reading walks every service directory rather than the diff, so an obligation missing since a service shipped is found in the first wave after the contract named it. The contract itself is a file in the same checkout, so its version is the commit it was last changed in and no separate record is needed.

examples.title: A bank project reading its services against the declared money path contract
examples.notes: The reference this contract shape comes from declares its obligations one per row with the gate that enforces each: a pure domain layer that may not import a framework (ADR-0002, gate `domain-purity-gate`), a published `openapi.yaml` on its own version axis (ADR-0048, gates `api-contract-gate` and `openapi-route-conformance`), a forward migration carrying an in file rollback note (gate `db-migration-gate`), an idempotency key on every write (gate `idempotency-coverage-money-path`), a transactional outbox rather than an inline publish (ADR-0003, gate `outbox-has-writer`), an injected clock (gate `clock-injection-gate`), a threat model (ADR-0030 D2, gate `threat-model-coverage`), a runbook (gate `service-runbook-drift`) and a self declaration (ADR-0071, gate `governance-manifest`). Two lessons carry over regardless of the technology. Where a gate already answers an obligation, the reading should not spend judgement on it, and where none exists the reading is the only thing standing between the contract and the wave. And the reference's gates each declare how many subjects they expect to find, which is the same instinct as this recipe's census: a certification that read three of eleven services is not a lighter certification, it is a different and much weaker claim.

examples.title: The project's own backlog as the backlog role
examples.notes: Filing a gap as an item rather than repairing it is what keeps the certification honest, and it also feeds the delivery work that already exists: an item filed here is carried by whatever charter delivers accepted items, under review, with its own gates. The ageing count in the fourth outcome is only computable because the earlier gaps are rows in the same place rather than sentences in an old report.

inputSchema.name: project_id
inputSchema.description: The project whose services are certified. The census is the whole project, never one service, because an obligation missing everywhere reads as normal when only one service is examined.

inputSchema.name: wave_ref
inputSchema.description: The wave about to merge, by whatever identifier this project gives a wave. Empty means certify the project as it currently stands, which is the self paced pass rather than the blocking one.

inputSchema.name: contract_version
inputSchema.description: Pin the certification to a named version of the declared contract. Empty means read the version currently in force, which is the normal case; a pin is for re reading an old wave with the standard it was actually judged by.
